transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um, so I came in because... well, people keep telling me they can’t really follow what I’m trying to explain lately. Like, I'll be writing my artist statements, or typing up client notes, or even just talking in meetings, and I guess I start jumping around a lot? 

I'll go from talking about the textures of the piece—which, actually, I just found this incredible raw linen supplier over on 4th street. The owner has this ancient orange cat that just sleeps on the bolts of fabric all day. It’s adorable, but it sheds everywhere, so I literally spent an hour lint-rolling my last commission before I could even prime it. But, um, anyway... I'll be talking about the textures, and then I jump straight to the budgets, and then into the secret meanings behind the colors, and... I don't know, people just get lost and say they don't understand me.
Over the past week or two, have you noticed your mood being unusually high, elated, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual?

Yeah, I guess I have. Like, for stretches lately I’ll just feel completely lit up and almost unstoppable. It’s like every single idea I have is just brilliant. But then... I don't know, a tiny comment from a collaborator can make me snap in a way that feels way bigger than the situation. 

Like my friend Sarah, we're working on this installation together, and she said something about the lighting being too harsh, and I just completely lost it on her. Which is weird because Sarah and I usually get along perfectly. We actually met in a ceramics class back when I was getting my undergrad. She made this really hideous, lopsided vase that she insisted on glazing this awful seafoam green color. And the kiln actually broke the day they fired it. Not because of her vase, obviously, but we always joked that her art was cursed. The instructor was so mad about the kiln, he had this weird little mustache that would literally twitch when he got angry... um. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my mood. But yeah, I've just been feeling really, really charged up like that, but also kind of ready to bite someone's head off if they interrupt my flow.

Has this feeling of being 'lit up,' high-energy, and quick to snap been a noticeable change from how you normally are, lasting nearly every day for a week or more, or is this more how you've felt on and off since you were young?

Well, it's definitely a change. Like, I haven't been this way my whole life. The whole feeling energized and irritable, not sleeping much, doing a million projects at once... that's been happening for, I'd say, about 10 months now. 

Which actually reminds me, 10 months ago was right around the time I started that massive mural project downtown. The one by the old bakery? They have the absolute best sourdough there, by the way. The baker, this guy named Tomas, he gets up at like 3 AM every single day to start the dough. I don't know how he does it. I mean, I guess I've been up at 3 AM a lot lately too, but I'm usually painting, not baking. Tomas actually offered to teach me how to make a sourdough starter once, but I read that you have to feed it every day, and honestly, keeping myself fed is hard enough right now. Plus, my apartment gets really drafty in the winter, and I heard starters need a warm environment to thrive. My landlord is supposed to fix the weather stripping on my windows, but he's been dodging my calls for weeks... 

Um, but yeah, to answer your question, this isn't how I've always been. It's been going on for about 10 months.

Before this 10-month period started, had you ever experienced a separate time—lasting a week or more—where you felt persistently depressed, low, or lost interest in things, or a similar period of unusually high energy and elevated mood?

Um... before the 10 months? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal days where I'm just tired or whatever, but nothing like a whole week of being super depressed or totally wired like I am now. 

Actually, before all this started, I was in a pretty steady routine. I was going to this yoga studio down the block from my place. The instructor there, she was super intense about breathwork. Like, she would walk around and literally put her hand on your ribs to make sure you were expanding enough. It was kind of invasive, honestly? But she had this playlist that was all just... like, whale sounds mixed with ambient synth. I actually tried to find it on Spotify later because I thought it would be really good background noise for when I'm mixing resin. Resin is so finicky, you know? If you mix it too fast, you get all these micro-bubbles, and then you have to use a heat gun to pop them, but if you hold the heat gun too close, you can scorch the piece. I ruined a whole batch of coasters that way last Christmas. I was making them as gifts for my family, but they ended up looking like they had some kind of weird skin disease... 

Wait, sorry. No, I haven't really had any periods like that before this started.

During these past 10 months of feeling this way, have you experienced anything unusual like hearing voices or sounds others don't hear, or having beliefs—like feeling you have special powers or a special mission—that others find hard to believe?

Well, yeah, actually. When I'm in one of those really intense zones, you know, staying up all night and juggling a million things, I... I start noticing things. Like, really specific things. The paint stains on my drop cloths, or even just random phrases in spam emails—I've been completely sure they're, like, sending me instructions. Telling me what to create next. 

And emails are so weird anyway, right? Like, who even reads half the stuff we get? My inbox is a total disaster. I signed up for this newsletter about sustainable foraging last year, because I thought maybe I could make my own pigments from, like, berries and roots. I saw this documentary about a guy in Japan who does that, and it was beautiful. He lived in this tiny wooden house in the mountains. I'd love to live in the mountains, but I'm terrified of bears. Did you know black bears can run like 35 miles an hour? That's faster than Usain Bolt. So, foraging is probably out for me, honestly. 

But anyway, yeah, the instructions from the stains and the emails. And... sometimes I hear this woman's voice in my studio. Just sort of commenting on what I'm doing. It usually happens when I'm super charged up and barely sleeping.
Do you ever hear that woman's voice or feel that things are sending you special messages when you're NOT in one of these high-energy, wired periods—like when your mood and sleep are back to normal?

Yeah, actually. There was this one stretch... I think it was maybe a month where things kind of quieted down. I was actually sleeping a normal amount, like getting a solid eight hours, and I didn't have that crazy unstoppable energy pushing me. But even then, for a few weeks during that time, I was still hearing her. She'd be making comments from behind my supply shelves. And I was still seeing those hidden warnings in my studio materials, like the way the bristles on my brushes were drying. 

Speaking of brushes, I really need to invest in some good sable ones. The synthetic ones just don't hold water the same way, you know? They fray so fast, especially if you don't clean them with the right soap. I found this artisan brush soap at a craft fair last summer—it smelled exactly like lavender and cedar. The woman selling it was wearing this incredible hand-knit sweater, like, really chunky wool. I tried knitting once, but I could never keep the tension right. My scarves always ended up looking like they had tumors or something. It's so frustrating when your hands just won't do what your brain wants them to do. Like, you can see the finished thing in your head, but the translation gets all garbled. 

But, um, yeah. Even when I was feeling totally normal and sleeping fine, the voice and the messages were still there for a few weeks.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a 10-month period of manic symptoms (elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, flight of ideas, distractibility, tangential speech) meeting criteria for a manic episode. During these manic periods, she also experiences psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of a woman's voice, delusional beliefs that emails/objects send her special instructions). Critically, these psychotic symptoms persisted for several weeks during a period when mood and sleep had normalized, confirming that hallucinations/delusions occur independent of mood episodes for a substantial duration (≥2 weeks), which is the key distinguishing feature from a mood disorder with psychotic features (F30.2/F31.2). Since mood episodes appear to account for the majority of the illness course and no distinct chronic psychotic-only history predates the mood symptoms, and the psychotic symptoms occurred both during and outside mood episodes, this best fits Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0).
